scope: Shared runtime change verification. Protocol fixtures and actual existing-game compatibility are separate; this does not publish or replace any existing APK and does not increase the completed-game count.

protocol.scope: Deterministic Chromium protocol fixtures with manually advanced RAF, instrumented model and controlled native phone snapshots. Not gameplay, performance or physical hardware evidence.

tests.name: Default games retain one-frame Enter A behavior
Opt-in DOM Enter stays held and releases as A
Opt-in native Enter down/up preserves held A
Coalesced opt-in Enter tap survives zero-physics frames exactly once
Holding the menu confirm and DOM repeat cannot create a game A
Pause cancels held keyboard A; repeat cannot rearm before keyup
Remote A/B held across pause stay quarantined until raw release
Connected phone cancelSeq distinguishes cancellation from ordinary release
CancelSeq change with a still-held remote button cannot restore that hold
First phone connection establishes a cancelSeq baseline without cancelling local input
CancelSeq wrap/reset is detected rather than ignored as a lower value
Phone disconnect freezes the model and permits independent keyboard takeover
Fresh phone hold sampled in the resume frame cannot bypass clearInput
Cancellation survives zero-step RAF frames and reaches all substeps of its owned sample
Retry clears held keyboard input and ignores its later DOM repeats

existingGameCompatibility.scope: Ordinary browser input using the existing Magnetic Warehouse model/art and the candidate shared runtime. Resources come from a separate local unsigned compatibility build, not the previously published signed APK.

checks.name: P freezes gameplay state and tick, P resumes
R restarts with clean simulation state
resizing keeps canvas and complete sidebar text visible
no page, console or resource errors

limitations: Protocol tests advance RAF deliberately and use an instrumented model; they are not timing-performance measurements.
The compatibility run uses ordinary game inputs in Chromium. No physical TV, phone or Android installation is claimed.
